newsitem.title: USA: Northern Border pipeline approved by FERC.
newsitem.headline: Northern Border pipeline approved by FERC.

text.p: Northern Border Pipeline Co said Wednesday that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approved the construction of Northern Border's Chicago Project, finding the project to be "in the public convenience and necessity."

Northern Border, which is 70 percent owned by Northern Border Partners LP, said the FERC also approved the provisions of the settlement agreement for Northern Border's most recent rate case, which was filed in October of 1996.

The Chicago Project, an $837 million expansion and extension of the Northern Border system, will bring an additional 700 million cubic feet of Canadian natural gas into U.S. markets. The project involves the construction by Northern Border of about 390 miles of 30- and 36-inch diameter pipe and the addition of 303,500 horsepower of compression, the company said.

"The settlement, achieved with the support of Northern Border's customers, resolves several complex issues and provides additional rate certainty and the economic underpinning for The Chicago Project, " Northern Border president Larry DeRoin said in a news release.
